# Draft:Christ the King Episcopal Church (Valdosta)

----
Christ the King is an Episcopal church in Valdosta, Georgia.
The formerly independent congregation was covered in national media, when it sought membership within the Episcopal Church.  At the time the Valdosta church was led by Rev. Stan White, a former Pentecostal clergyman. More than two hundred parishioners were confirmed in one service, and the church was received by Bishop Harry Shipps as a new congregation of the Episcopal Diocese of Georgia. In September 1990, Christianity Today featured the congregation's journey in a cover story entitled, "Why the Bishops Went to Valdosta", spawning similar coverage in Charisma Magazine, the Christian Century, and the Living Church. Randall Balmer discussed the church in his book "Mine Eyes Have Seen the Glory: A Journey into the Evangelical Subculture of America" as well as in a 1993 PBS Documentary series of the same name. The event stands as an example of the Convergence Movement in Christianity. In 2000, Stan White was featured as a guest on NPR's Talk of the Nation.
Christ the King has been in its current geographical location since 2021.
